→ D2 (concedes): Conceded as to timing and form: F8 and F9 are both timestamped 22:51 and the complete chat record (F10) places them before the 22:54 segment start in F3, so the rider's own message F9 is valid pre-segment consent and I do not build any claim on the statement F11. → D3: The opponent's own reading confirms my case: a yes to a named road covers only driving on that road, and no fact ties the 22:54–23:03 segment (F3) to Guillemard Road — no stop, no locating message, no road name in the GPS facts — so under G13 the segment is named_road_untied/undetermined, not exempted, and if that affects the amount the case goes to a human (RD-5). [F3 F8 F9 F10] [RD-5]
→ D4: The congestion reason fails as evidence for this segment: F12 shows the PIE at band 2 only for 22:32–22:54 and F15 records no incident at all, while F3's segment runs 22:54–23:03, so nothing corroborates a reasonable cause targeting the replaced stretch of the optimal route (RD-4(a), RD-4(b) is corroboration only). [F12 F15 F3] [RD-4]

[F15 F12 F13 F14 F3] [RD-4 RD-2]
→ D6: I accept the metered framework but not the arithmetic: the refund is the unexempted segment's extra_km, 2.13 km (F3), at this trip's own rate $1.4102/km derived from $19.15 ÷ 13.58 km (F7, F4) = $3.00, not the billed 2.59 km figure; the $0.11 waiting unit (F5) is a metered waiting-time unit and stays with the driver. claims.assertion: The trip ran 13.6 km against an optimal route of 11.0 km, 2.6 km (24%) longer, and the fare was metered (RydeTAXI), so extra kilometres went straight into what my client paid: $19.15 of the $32.28 charged was distance.
There is exactly one off-route segment, 22:54–23:03, in which 3.77 km was driven where the optimal route covers only 1.64 km, adding 2.13 km and reaching up to 1095 m off the optimal route.

The rider did agree to the named road Guillemard Road before the segment began — the driver asked 'mind if I go round via Guillemard Road?' at 22:51 and the rider replied 'Sure, go ahead.' at 22:51 (F8, F9), both timestamps earlier than the segment start of 22:54.

However, no record ties the driven off-route segment to Guillemard Road: there is no stop on Guillemard Road, no message placing the car on it, and no road name fact for it, so on the record the agreed named road and the 1095 m excursion are not connected and the segment's coverage is undetermined.
The driver's claim that the rider agreed to the Guillemard Road turn is a post-trip statement (F11), not consent; consent can only come from the rider's own pre-segment message, which here is F9.

No traffic incident near the route was recorded during the trip (F15), and the only band-1/2 record is the PIE at band 2 (10–19 km/h) for 22:32–22:54 (F12), which does not cover the 22:54–23:03 segment and does not concern the replaced stretch of the optimal route, so a band record alone cannot excuse the detour.

Because the detour is unexcused, on this metered RydeTAXI trip the refund is the detour kilometres at this trip's own per-km rate: 2.13 km × $1.4102/km = $3.00, the per-km rate being derived from the fare facts ($19.15 ÷ 13.58 km) and applied to the 2.13 extra km in F3.

Only the waiting-time unit (F5, $0.11) is charged for the in-trip stop and is kept; no other surcharge appears beyond ERP/tolls, waiting, destination change, cancellation and platform fee, and no surge applies (F6).
The driver has 2 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days, so this case makes the conduct repeated and supports an account-review action on top of the refund.

weaknesses: The rider's own message F9 ('Sure, go ahead.') is a clear agreement to the named road Guillemard Road and was sent at 22:51, before the segment start of 22:54 — the driver will cite F8/F9/F3 to say the detour is covered by RD-5 and should be no_action.

The traffic record does help the driver's story: the PIE was at band 2 (10–19 km/h) at 22:32–22:54 (F12), so he can argue the reroute had a reasonable basis and was not an arbitrary errand; my client's only answer is that F12 does not cover the 22:54–23:03 segment and F15 records no incident.

My refund figure is small ($3.00) and rests on the 2.13 km in F3; the rider may have hoped for a larger 'difference from estimate' sum, but 2.6 km total excess (F1) against a 2.59 km billed excess (F4) leaves nothing beyond the metered excess, and the rider's 90-day record shows 0 upheld disputes (F17), so no pattern argument exists on the rider side.

claims.assertion: The only off-route segment on the record is F3 (22:54–23:03, 3.77 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.64 km, +2.13 km, up to 1095 m off the optimal route); the ride is otherwise measured at 13.6 km vs 11.0 km optimal (F1) over 29.8 min vs 20.7 min estimated (F2).

Before that segment began, the driver asked the rider for consent to a named route — 'mind if I go round via Guillemard Road?' (F8, 22:51) — and the rider replied 'Sure, go ahead.' (F9, 22:51); both messages are timestamped and the chat record is complete (F10), so consent predates the segment start of 22:54 in F3.

The agreement is to a named road (Guillemard Road, F8), so on the face of the exchanged words the segment of F3 is covered by a specified-route authorisation; the record contains no fact naming Guillemard Road on the driven path, so the tie between the agreed road and the segment is not itself established by a record.

The driver's reason for the route was congestion on the optimal corridor: the Pan Island Expressway was recorded at speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) from 22:32 to 22:54 (F12), the very hour before and at the start of the deviation in F3, and the statement in F11 repeats that same reason.

No traffic incident (Accident/Roadwork/Heavy Traffic etc.) is recorded near the route during the trip window (F15) and there is no incident fact tied to the replaced stretch of the optimal route, so the RD-4(a) exemption is not available on this record; the band-2 reading in F12 and the band-3 readings on Braddell Road and KPE (F13, F14) remain corroboration only, consistent with the driver's diversion being a reasonable response to congestion rather than an errand of his own.

This is a metered RydeTAXI trip, so any refund is limited to metered distance; the billed excess distance is $3.65 (2.59 km × $1.4102/km) as against the 2.13 km excess in F3, and the waiting item is a metered 0.4 min = $0.11 (F5), with no surge (F6) and no unpublished add-on in the breakdown (F7).

The driver has 2 route disputes upheld in the last 90 days (F18), so if the judge finds the segment of F3 unexempted, the only additional consequence available is that the repeated-offence flag attaches — the profile facts (F17, F18) cannot by themselves establish that the deviation in F3 was unexempted.
Nothing in the chat (F8, F9, F11) or elsewhere in the record is a threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so the safety escalation route is not engaged by this material.

weaknesses: The rider will press RD-4(a): there is no traffic-incident fact for this trip (F15), and band readings alone do not exempt a segment under RD-4(b), so the driver's congestion reason in F11 has no accepted corroboration targeting the replaced stretch of the optimal route.

The rider will press RD-5/G13: the consent in F8–F9 names Guillemard Road, but nothing in the record ties the driven segment of F3 to Guillemard Road (no stop, no locating message, no road name in the GPS facts), so the segment may be found undetermined and referred to a human rather than exempted.

The rider will cite F3 itself: 3.77 km driven against 1.64 km optimal, adding 2.13 km and straying up to 1095 m from the optimal route, with F1 showing +2.6 km (+24%) and F2 showing +9.1 min — a large, one-sided deviation on a metered fare that RD-2/RD-1 read against the driver.

The rider will cite F4–F7: $3.65 of excess distance was actually billed and appears in the metered total of $32.28, so the exposure is a partial refund of up to about $3.65 plus, on a strict reading, the $0.11 metered waiting item in F5.

points.response: Accepted as a statement of the record: there is one off-route segment (F3) on a metered trip of 13.6 km vs 11.0 km optimal and 29.8 min vs 20.7 min estimated (F1, F2), which is exactly why RD-1's no-threshold obligation bites.

Conceded as to timing and form: F8 and F9 are both timestamped 22:51 and the complete chat record (F10) places them before the 22:54 segment start in F3, so the rider's own message F9 is valid pre-segment consent and I do not build any claim on the statement F11.

The opponent's own reading confirms my case: a yes to a named road covers only driving on that road, and no fact ties the 22:54–23:03 segment (F3) to Guillemard Road — no stop, no locating message, no road name in the GPS facts — so under G13 the segment is named_road_untied/undetermined, not exempted, and if that affects the amount the case goes to a human (RD-5).

The congestion reason fails as evidence for this segment: F12 shows the PIE at band 2 only for 22:32–22:54 and F15 records no incident at all, while F3's segment runs 22:54–23:03, so nothing corroborates a reasonable cause targeting the replaced stretch of the optimal route (RD-4(a), RD-4(b) is corroboration only).

I agree RD-4(a) is unavailable on this record, and that is precisely the point: with the incident exemption gone and band data insufficient alone, the F3 segment must be treated under RD-2 rather than excused as 'reasonable response to congestion'; the 1095 m excursion in F3 is far beyond a corridor change.

I accept the metered framework but not the arithmetic: the refund is the unexempted segment's extra_km, 2.13 km (F3), at this trip's own rate $1.4102/km derived from $19.15 ÷ 13.58 km (F7, F4) = $3.00, not the billed 2.59 km figure; the $0.11 waiting unit (F5) is a metered waiting-time unit and stays with the driver.

Agreed that F17/F18 cannot establish the deviation; but the deviation is established by F1 and F3 and left unexempted by the failed RD-4 and unproven RD-5 tie, so RD-6's flag applies because the driver already has 2 upheld route disputes (F18).

No safety escalation is claimed; F8, F9 and F11 contain no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 are not engaged and the case stays with the ordinary route-deviation rules.

Conceded as to the arithmetic of the record: F1 gives 13.6 km against 11.0 km optimal and F7 shows $19.15 of the $32.28 was distance on a metered RydeTAXI trip — but fare size alone is not the test; RD-2 sizes any refund only from the unexempted segment's extra_km, i.e. F3's 2.13 km, not from the whole +2.6 km in F1.

Conceded: F3 is the only off-route segment on the record (22:54–23:03, 3.77 km driven against 1.64 km optimal, +2.13 km, up to 1095 m off route), and it is the sole segment RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 need to be applied to.

Agreed, and it is the core of my case: the rider's own message F9 ('Sure, go ahead.') at 22:51 answers the driver's ask in F8 ('mind if I go round via Guillemard Road?'), both timestamped inside a complete record (F10) and both earlier than the 22:54 segment start in F3, so RD-5 consent exists before the segment.

I accept the segment cannot be tied to Guillemard Road by any record fact — there is no stop, no message placing the car on it, no road-name fact — and my brief already states the ground as named_road_untied (G13); but an untied segment means undetermined, not unexempted, so it cannot be auto-refunded, and RD-5 sends an undetermined segment that affects money to a human, i.e. escalate, not refund_partial.

Conceded: F11 is a post-trip driver statement and, under RD-5 as read with G11, a driver's assertion of agreement is not itself consent; I rely only on the rider's own pre-segment message F9, quoted by its id.

Conceded that RD-4(a) fails for want of any incident fact (F15) and that RD-4(b) cannot exempt a segment on its own; F12 (PIE band 2, 10–19 km/h, 22:32–22:54) remains in the record as corroboration that the corridor the driver rerouted around was congested, which is why RD-4(c) leaves only the RD-2 computation and not a further penalty.

The rider's $3.00 overshoots: RD-2 multiplies the unexempted segment's extra_km by the trip's per-km rate, but F3's 2.13 km is the detour excess while F4 shows the billed excess distance is 2.59 km = $3.65, and the rider's own figure misapplies $1.4102/km to the 2.13 km; in any event nothing is refundable while the segment's coverage (F8, F9 to a named road) is undetermined, so the honest ceiling is $3.65 only if the judge first finds the segment unexempted.

Agreed: F5's $0.11 is a metered waiting unit on a RydeTAXI trip and is kept, and no undisclosed surcharge exists — F6 shows surge 1.0× and F7's breakdown is base, distance, time, waiting and platform fee only, so FARE-1 produces nothing to refund.

F18 (2 upheld route disputes in 90 d) cannot be used to make the deviation in F3 unexempted; RD-6 makes a profile fact available only as an additional action once the case is already made out against the driver, and the rider side's own figures leave the case undetermined, so no flag_account should attach here.
